sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 99. Whoever buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine

sections.heading: Essential ingredients
sections.body: Whoever buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine

sections.heading: Explanations
sections.body:
Explanation 1.—Any prostitute or any person keeping or managing a brothel, who buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of a female under the age of eighteen years shall, until the contrary is proved, be presumed to have obtained possession of such female with the intent that she shall be used for the purpose of prostitution
Explanation 2.—“Illicit intercourse” has the same meaning as in section 98

learningObjectives: Master the offence of buying, hiring, or obtaining possession of a child for prostitution or illicit intercourse under BNS s. 99.
Recognize the severe statutory minimum sentence of seven years extending up to fourteen years and fine.
Understand the statutory presumption under Explanation 1 against brothel keepers and prostitutes obtaining possession of minors.
Appreciate the asymmetry in sentencing between buyer (s. 99) and seller (s. 98).
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 99 penalizes whoever buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Suppresses commercial child sexual exploitation by imposing severe mandatory minimum sentences of seven to fourteen years on buyers and procurers of minors.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 99 (corresponding to IPC s. 373).
Actus reus: Buying, hiring, or otherwise obtaining possession of any child (under eighteen years).
Mens rea: Intent or knowledge that the child will at any age be employed or used for prostitution, illicit intercourse, or any unlawful and immoral purpose.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description not less than seven years extending up to fourteen years, and fine.
Explanation 1: Presumption of intent when a prostitute or brothel keeper buys, hires, or obtains possession of a female under eighteen.
Explanation 2: 'Illicit intercourse' has the same meaning as in Section 98.
essentialIngredients: The person bought or obtained is a child (under eighteen years of age).
The accused bought, hired, or otherwise obtained possession of the child.
The accused acted with intent or knowledge that the child would at any age be employed or used for prostitution, illicit intercourse, or any unlawful and immoral purpose.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 99 targets the demand side of child trafficking and commercial sexual exploitation. It penalizes anyone who buys, hires, or otherwise obtains possession of a child under eighteen for prostitution or immoral purposes. In BNS 2023, the legislature significantly strengthened the sentencing framework: while the seller under s. 98 faces up to ten years imprisonment, the buyer under s. 99 faces a mandatory minimum sentence of seven years which may extend to fourteen years imprisonment, alongside fine. This reflects a deliberate legislative determination to crush the financial demand that fuels child trafficking. Explanation 1 creates a statutory presumption of unlawful intent against any prostitute or brothel keeper who obtains possession of a female under eighteen.
examples: Teaching example (Brothel owner buying a minor): A brothel manager pays money to purchase a fifteen-year-old girl and takes physical custody of her. Under Explanation 1, the law presumes the manager obtained possession with intent to use her for prostitution. The manager faces a mandatory minimum sentence of seven years up to fourteen years under s. 99.

Teaching example (Hiring a child for immoral purposes): An accused enters into a contract paying a monthly fee to keep a seventeen-year-old child in his private residence for non-marital sexual relations. This constitutes hiring/obtaining possession for illicit intercourse under s. 99.
distinctions: Section 99 vs Section 98: Section 98 penalizes the seller/disposer (up to 10 years); Section 99 penalizes the buyer/receiver with an enhanced mandatory minimum of seven to fourteen years.
Section 99 vs Section 95: Section 95 penalizes hiring a child to commit an offence; Section 99 specifically penalizes buying or obtaining possession for prostitution or illicit intercourse.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether a brothel keeper caught taking custody of a sixteen-year-old girl can claim she was hired only as a domestic cleaning maid.
Rule: Under Explanation 1 to BNS s. 99, a person keeping or managing a brothel who obtains possession of a female under eighteen is presumed to have obtained her with intent for prostitution.
Application: The accused is a brothel manager and took possession of a female minor; the statutory presumption applies and cannot be rebutted by mere unsubstantiated assertions.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 99 and faces seven to fourteen years imprisonment.
